steps.caption_md: Computing `fib(5)` bottom-up. Start with the two base values `prev = fib(0) = 0` and `cur = fib(1) = 1`. No recursion tree, no stack growth: just two variables.
Iteration `i = 2`: new `cur = 0 + 1 = 1`, and `prev` takes the old `cur`. We now hold `fib(1) = 1` and `fib(2) = 1`.
Iteration `i = 3` is next. The naive recursion would reach `fib(3)` many times; here it is computed once.

predict.prompt_md: Currently `prev = 1` and `cur = 1`. After the `i = 3` update, what are `prev` and `cur`?
predict.explanation_md: The update is simultaneous: `prev` becomes the old `cur` (1) and `cur` becomes `prev + cur = 1 + 1 = 2`. Option b would overwrite `prev` with the new sum, and c would mean nothing changed.

steps.caption_md: Iteration `i = 3` gives `prev = 1`, `cur = 2`, so `fib(3) = 2`. Total work so far: 2 additions.
Iteration `i = 5`: `cur = 2 + 3 = 5`, so `fib(5) = 5`. That took 4 additions for n = 5 (about n steps, O(n) time) and held only 2 numbers (O(1) space). The naive tree for `fib(5)` has 15 calls.
